D012-D018_h002.question:
Alright, doc, thanks for seeing me. It's… I don't know, it feels a bit silly, but it's gotten to the point where it’s really messing with my head, and my wife says I'm not myself. It's been going on for a few months now, seems to have cropped up after that pile-up on the interstate. We were jammed in there for hours, the air thick with smoke, bodies... you know.

Anyway, ever since then, I just can't stand being in tight spots. Tunnels, elevators, even just a packed room – my heart starts hammering, I get all sweaty, can't breathe. It just hits me out of nowhere, this overwhelming fear, like I'm trapped and can't get out. I used to be fine, even with all the tight spaces we dealt with on the job. Now, I find myself avoiding certain routes to work, taking the stairs instead of the lift, even if it means lugging my gear up ten flights. It’s starting to affect my calls, too, making me hesitate, and that’s just not me. I’m a rescue worker, for crying out loud. I can't be like this.

    D. Specific Phobia

I’ve noticed similar feelings when I hear really loud, unexpected noises, or even when I see little kids in those elaborate Halloween costumes around campus. It's ridiculous, I know, but it’s real. It started not long after that incident with the building collapse on campus, when I was there for a late-night meeting. Thankfully, I was unharmed, but it was quite a shock.
